research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from talent and playing-time counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
play-by-play derived possession records as a basis for role and outcome measures
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and counts once talent is controlled?
Does talent control behave adequately when talent is confounded with team quality and role assignment?
How are organizer, shaper and terminal roles operationalised and validated, and are they independent of the outcome they are meant to explain?
Is the number of team-seasons (90) and lineup cells sufficient for within-team and talent-adjusted contrasts?

historical_evidence.finding: Lineup- and play-type-specific suppression profiles of stars were examined on NBA play-by-play possessions and reconstructed lineups. Verdict 'rank-1 suppressor varies meaningfully across players'; rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control recorded.

Series-level AVOID share versus winning: game-level rho=-0.19 (p=0.008) was flagged as inflated n and team-quality confounded; series-level rho=-0.26 (p=0.07, n=50) was underpowered, with about 80 series stated as needed for p<0.05. Still confounded by team quality.

Absence validation: real absences moved the association structure (V1a 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1b CONFIRMED), but the simulation-magnitude tests V2a (rho=+0.288, p=0.077) and V2b (rho=+0.253, p=0.115) failed, attributed to small sample.

Residual structural influence is not reducible to usage (F1a residual share about 0.90-0.93) and the usage-residual is a split-half-stable player property (F1b pooled rho about +0.67 to +0.69). Measure reliability was flagged as a limitation.

Team offensive association structure is more similar across split halves than across teams (P1a) and is not reducible to play-type rates (P1b; residual R2=0.043). This concerns team structure, not lineup role coverage.
Elite creator to teammate PPP at lags 1-3 gave a clean null with adequate power (Jokic lag-1 n=1880, ATT +0.0282, CI [-0.043, +0.099]), so no lineup-matched teammate-PPP lift was found at any lag.
Playoff pivot-pair sustainability: 10/12 pairs consistent and within 0.10 of non-pivot; two pairs with enough signal were PIVOT_LOSES. Adequately powered null for pivoting producing higher PPP.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type was reported as descriptive lineup PPP gaps (for example Jokic vs MIN 0.814, n=59; Giannis forced PULL_UP gap). No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Opponent play before the star: PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars, with n_after 32-95 for several cells. No multiplicity correction was recorded.

Sequence-memory horizon on n=1,024,980 possessions: effective horizon about 2-3 possessions, with absolute AUC only about 0.591. Time-split validation was used. Relates to the possession data, not to role coverage.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether a play-type-derived behavioural share predicts winning while separating it from team quality.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as underpowered at series level (n=50, p=0.07) and confounded by team quality; game-level significance was inflated by non-independent observations.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Validating simulated magnitudes of structural change under real absences.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as small-sample failure (V2a and V2b not significant, wide CIs). The V1 direction test did pass.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking lineup and play-type suppressors per star without multiplicity control.
failed_approaches.why: Rank-1 deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control; an OTHER artifact was flagged in the doc.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing star-specific lineup and forced-play-type suppression.
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching was done; later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts. The recorded failure mechanism is unclear.

evidence_establishes: Possession-level play-by-play data can support adequately powered null and positive tests of lineup-linked and sequence-linked efficiency questions (FAM:SF-APPS-074, FAM:SF-APPS-059, FAM:SF18, FAM:SF17).
Talent and team-quality confounding has already been recorded as a central threat in comparable influence analyses (FAM:SF-CHT-039, FAM:SF-APPM-022).
Small cell and small unit counts have repeatedly left absence-magnitude and series-level tests underpowered (FAM:SF20, FAM:SF-CHT-039).
Residual-influence measures have shown reproducibility (FAM:SF18), which is relevant to whether talent can be partialled out.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record defines or tests organizer, shaper or terminal roles, or lineup coverage of those roles.
No retrieved record tests whether role coverage is separable from talent and playing-time counts within teams.
No retrieved record reports a talent-control specification that behaves adequately for lineup-level role coverage.
No retrieved record gives a validated measure of lineup role coverage or its reliability across team-seasons.
Nothing here shows whether 90 team-seasons provide enough within-team variation in coverage for the contrast.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a structural-definition question. Its first step is operational definition of roles, and the retrieved evidence does not supply one.
Role labels derived from the same possessions used for the outcome (PPP or influence) risk circularity; this is the outcome-derived-label concern.
Talent is likely collinear with role membership (stars are the usual organizers and terminals), so separability depends on within-player or within-lineup variation that may be thin.
A 90 team-season unit count is small for talent-adjusted regression with several role terms; lineup- or possession-level units with team-season clustering would be needed.
The retrieved records suggest the same kinds of threat (confounding, multiplicity, small cells, placebo dependence) that a competent test here would need to address.
uncertainties: Whether role coverage has been defined and validated in earlier project work outside the retrieved records is unknown.
The exact talent proxy available in the data is not established; the data description lists no player-rating or talent field.
The shares of possessions with identifiable organizer, shaper and terminal actions are unknown.
Reliability of role labels across seasons and split halves is unknown.
Retrieved records are summaries; several were cut and point to read_family for full text, which was not read.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not test the question, but they show that talent confounding, small units, underpowered series-level or cell-level tests, and missing multiplicity control have repeatedly undermined comparable influence claims in this project. That history, together with the absence of any role definition in the retrieved evidence, moves the decision from proceed toward do_not_proceed until the role definition, talent control and unit design are specified.

blocking_constraints.text: Organizer, shaper and terminal labels would be derived from the same play-by-play possessions that define the efficiency outcome, so coverage and outcome can be circular.
Talent (star usage and quality) is likely collinear with role membership. No talent proxy is specified, and team quality confounds team-season comparisons (FAM:SF-CHT-039).
90 team-seasons is small for talent-adjusted contrasts across several role terms; FAM:SF20 and FAM:SF-CHT-039 were underpowered at comparable scale.
No reliability evidence is recorded for role coverage measures; reproducibility is shown only for other constructs (FAM:SF18).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record addresses organizer, shaper or terminal lineup coverage or its separability from talent. Related work covers lineup- and play-type-specific suppression (inconclusive, no multiplicity control), team-quality-confounded behavioural shares (untestable), absence-validation magnitudes (underpowered), residual influence reproducibility (supported), and null lineup-linked PPP lifts (rejected, adequately powered). These bear on the methods but do not answer the question.

risks.text: Role labels and the efficiency outcome both come from play-by-play possessions, so coverage effects may be partly mechanical.
Talent, usage and team quality confound role coverage; FAM:SF-CHT-039 shows this confound was not resolved in a comparable setting.
90 team-seasons and sparse role-by-lineup cells risk low power; FAM:SF20 and FAM:SF-CHT-039 were underpowered.
Several role terms and lineup cells across teams invite multiplicity; FAM:SF-APPM-022 and FAM:SF-APPA-050 had no correction.
No reliability for role coverage is recorded; split-half stability has been shown only for other measures (FAM:SF18).
Organizer, shaper and terminal actions may be rare for some lineups, leaving thin exposure in the cells needed for within-team contrasts.
FAM:SF-CHT-009 showed star-lineup gaps without placebo or matching, treated later as artifacts; a role-coverage effect without placebo would be similarly fragile.
Lineups with high coverage may be selected on prior performance or on coaching choice, so regression to the mean can mimic talent-adjusted effects.
Seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 and the partial 2025-26 files may differ in play style and role definitions, and FAM:SF-APPA-050 flagged drift.
Play-by-play action and sub-type classification may misassign roles; no label validation is recorded.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup-level coverage of at least one organizer, shaper or terminal role and possession-level PPP, adjusted for a pre-specified talent proxy, playing-time counts and team-season effects. Pre-registered before any analysis.
design.unit: Lineup-stint or possession, clustered by team-season and lineup. Team-season is used only as a grouping level, not as the unit.
design.sample: NBA regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 as the discovery set; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13 only) as the held-out confirmation. Playoffs excluded from the primary test. Partial 2025-26 files excluded.
design.power: Must be computed before analysis for the minimum detectable within-team coverage effect, given the lineup-cell counts after the exposure gate. If the gate leaves too few cells, the test is reported as untestable, not as a null.
design.controls: Talent proxy fixed in advance and computed from prior-season or out-of-sample data to avoid circularity; playing time and minutes; team-season fixed effects; opponent strength; lineup random effects. Role labels defined from pre-specified action rules and validated on a held-out labelled sample before use. Role coverage must not use the outcome possessions as its own label source (use a separate play-type definition or split-sample labelling).
design.falsification: Placebo role labels built from non-role play types and label-permutation nulls within team-season. The effect is treated as artifact if it survives only under the outcome-derived labels or fails placebo.
design.multiplicity: Single primary coefficient for coverage of at least one role, with the three individual roles and interactions as secondary. Holm correction across secondary contrasts.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary coefficient is positive with a CI excluding zero in the discovery set and replicates in the 2025-26 held-out regular season with the same sign, the placebo does not reproduce it, and talent-proxy stability is shown. Rejected if the CI excludes effects above the pre-specified minimum effect size. Otherwise uncertain. Untestable if the exposure gate or role-label validation fails.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files as listed (play-by-play, rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, box-score summary), with 2025-26 regular season used only after completion (2026-04-13). Playoffs and partial files excluded. Derived play-type possession graph used only after its build is documented and checked against raw play-by-play.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
